fender_blackface_deluxe.real: Fender Deluxe Reverb (blackface AB763, 1963–67; '65 Reissue and hand-wired '64 Custom), 22 W, 2×6V6, 1×12
fender_blackface_deluxe.voice: Scooped mids, glassy sparkling top, soft 6V6 lows; chimey clean that sags and compresses into smooth breakup early.

VOLUME.does: Non-master: VOLUME is the gain. Breakup starts ~3-4 with single coils; 6+ is the classic 6V6 overdrive. Louder = looser lows.

TREBLE.does: Strongest tone control of the scooped stack; adds sparkle and deepens the scoop. No MID knob (fixed 6.8k mid resistor).

BASS.does: Feeds lows into a small 6V6 power amp: gets flabby once VOLUME is up. Lower BASS as VOLUME rises.

INPUT.does: 1166/1167 only. Assumed input-jack select (real amp: jack 2 is about 6 dB quieter = more headroom). Not documented.

MODE.does: 1166/1167 only. Channel select: 1167 = Normal / Vibrato. 1166 presumably the '64 Custom's Normal / Bright.

model_notes.1094: Normal channel: no bright cap, one gain stage fewer; darker and cleaner, good for jazz lines and humbuckers. Legacy id (now 1167 MODE=Normal).
model_notes.1095: Vibrato channel: fixed 47 pF bright cap plus an extra gain stage; the one most people use; breaks up earlier. Legacy id (now 1167 MODE=Vibrato).
model_notes.1166: '64 Custom Deluxe Reverb: hand-wired modified AB763 with Bright and Normal channels. Added in CorOS 3.1.0.
model_notes.1167: '65 Deluxe Reverb reissue. MODE Normal/Vibrato reproduces 1094/1095. Preferred id for new presets.

boosts.why: Klon-style low-gain push adds the mids the scooped stack lacks without changing the amp's character; QC users run it at very low level.
Mid hump and compression fill the blackface scoop and trim the bass that makes the 6V6s flub.
Rat-type mids and compression suit scooped, uncompressed Fender-style amps.
QC forum users favour it (with Red Drive) for non-fizzy overdrive into the clean models.

cabs.why: The reissue's own 1×12 with Jensen C12K: glassy sparkle and attack.
Deluxe 1×12 with Eminence GA-SC64: alternative Deluxe speaker voicing.

known_for: Studio and club staple - 'on more recordings than any other Fender'
Country, blues, roots rock, soul, indie
Players listed for it: Duane Allman, Nile Rodgers, Dan Auerbach, John Scofield, Bill…
fender_blackface_deluxe.poor_at: Loud clean headroom, tight low end and high gain: 22 W of 6V6 flubs on the low E when pushed; scooped mids vanish in a dense mix.
fender_blackface_deluxe.watch_out: The low E distorts first (lots of bass reaches the power amp; speaker resonance 50-100 Hz). Cut BASS to 2-3 or high-pass 75-100 Hz before the amp once VOLUME is above ~4.

fender_blackface_twin.voice: Loud, piano-like clean: scooped mids, glassy to icy top, big firm lows; huge headroom and very little sag.

VOLUME.does: Non-master gain. The real amp stays clean to almost 6 where smaller Fenders break up at ~4; sounds thin when set very low.

BRIGHT.does: Bright cap across VOLUME: strong at low VOLUME, fades as VOLUME rises. Turn off if harsh or for squeaky-clean tones.

BASS.does: Plenty of lows on tap; turning it down keeps the amp tight and out of the bass guitar's range.

MID.does: Fills the mid scoop and raises level/drive. About 7 equals the fixed 6.8k mid of the smaller blackface amps.

TREBLE.does: Dominant control of the passive stack; adds glass and deepens the scoop.

model_notes.1083: Normal channel: no reverb-recovery stage, so it stays clean longest - the cleanest tube Fender here.
model_notes.1084: Vibrato channel: the extra stage of the reverb circuit makes it break up earlier than Normal.

boosts.why: Adds the midrange and compression this scooped, uncompressed amp lacks; the standard way to get lead tones from a Twin.
Rat-type distortion works on Fender-style scooped amps; the amp's headroom keeps it clear.
Low-gain mid push for edge-of-breakup without losing the Twin's clean punch.
Fat low end and strong mids suit mid-scooped amps.

cabs.why: The Twin Reverb's own open-back 2×12 with Jensens.
Twin 2×12 with Jensen C12K-2: efficient, glassy, big lows.
Fender cab with Celestion A-Type: rounder alternative if the Jensens are too icy.

known_for: The reference loud clean: country, jazz, funk, gospel, surf
Players listed for it: B.B. King, Johnny Marr, Eric Johnson (cleans), Steve Howe
fender_blackface_twin.poor_at: Natural breakup at sane volume and mid-forward lead tones without a pedal; thin and icy when VOLUME is very low.
fender_blackface_twin.watch_out: Painfully bright and bass-heavy by default: turn BRIGHT off and BASS down before touching TREBLE, and get overdrive from a pedal, not from VOLUME.

fender_blackface_super.real: Fender Super Reverb (blackface AB763, 1963–67; QC: '65), 40–45 W, 2×6L6, tube rectifier, 4×10
fender_blackface_super.voice: Big scooped Fender with punchy 4×10 attack: deep lows, screaming treble, low mids; comes alive past ~4.

VOLUME.does: Non-master gain; the amp 'comes alive' beyond 4. More VOLUME also means more bass and sharper treble.

BRIGHT.does: Bright cap across VOLUME; effect fades as VOLUME rises. Often off for the SRV-style 'magic six'.

BASS.does: The big cabinet makes lots of deep bass; keep around 2-3 when VOLUME is up.

MID.does: Vibrato model only (Normal has a fixed mid). Fills the scoop and adds push; the cure for 'lost in the mix'.

TREBLE.does: Dominant control of the passive stack; 4×10s are beamy, so high settings get piercing fast.

model_notes.1096: Normal channel: no MID knob, no reverb-recovery stage; cleaner.
model_notes.1097: Vibrato channel: adds MID and an extra gain stage; the usual choice.

boosts.why: The classic Texas-blues pairing: mid hump fills the scoop, trims bass and pushes the 6L6s.
Transparent boost for more sustain and harmonics at the amp's sweet spot (fenderguru's suggestion).
Low-gain mid lift that keeps the Super's punch.

cabs.why: 4×10 Jensen P10R - the same speaker type Fender fits to the Super Reverb reissue.
Oxford alnico 10s: softer, earlier-breaking vintage Fender 10-inch voice.

known_for: Blues players: Muddy Waters, Mike Bloomfield, Robert Cray, Derek Trucks
fender_blackface_super.poor_at: Mid-rich or tight high-gain tones; beamy, scooped and bass-heavy, so it gets lost or boomy if you just add VOLUME.
fender_blackface_super.watch_out: The scooped mids tempt you to turn up, which only adds more bass and sharp treble. Raise MID or add a mid-hump drive instead.

fender_blackface_princeton.voice: Small-box blackface: sweet chimey highs, punchy but soft lows; 'browner', mid-focused breakup that arrives early.

VOLUME.does: Non-master gain. With a Strat: 3-4 fairly clean, ~5 clean with balls, 7-8 trademark Fender overdrive.

TREBLE.does: Treble of a two-knob scooped stack (fixed 6.8k mid, no bright switch).

BASS.does: Dial it back: the small output section and 10-inch speaker fart out in the lows when pushed.

model_notes.1120: Reverb version: the reverb-recovery stage adds a gain stage, so it has more gain than a non-reverb Princeton.

boosts.why: Small mid push into an amp already on the edge; keeps the recording-amp sweetness.
Cuts the lows that make the Princeton fart out and adds mids for leads.
Clean boost with bass/treble shaping to tip the amp over without adding pedal distortion.

cabs.why: Princeton 1×10 with Jensen C10R, an original speaker type.
Princeton 1×10 with a Fat Jimmy C1060: fuller alternative 10.
A 12 gives wider, deeper lows when the 10 sounds boxy.

known_for: Studio/recording amp played on the verge of breakup
Ryan Adams; players listed for it: Bill Frisell, St. Vincent, Mac DeMarco, Gary Clark Jr.
Ancestor of the Mesa/Boogie Mark I
fender_blackface_princeton.poor_at: Clean headroom, tight bass and band-volume punch; the lows give up under heavy drive.
fender_blackface_princeton.watch_out: With humbuckers it overdrives very early and muddy: cut the level into the amp (Yek halves the input) and lower BASS before judging it.

fender_tweed_bassman.real: Fender Bassman 5F6-A (narrow-panel tweed, 1958–60; '59), 40–50 W, 2×6L6/5881, tube rectifier, 4×10
fender_tweed_bassman.voice: Raw, fat, warm tweed: big loose lows, thick mids, bright bite on the Bright channel; touch-sensitive breakup - the Marshall template.

VOLUME NORMAL.does: Gain of the darker, fatter Normal channel. In Patch models it blends in body and lows.

VOLUME BRIGHT.does: Gain of the Bright channel (more treble, most at low settings). In Patch models it supplies the bite.

TREBLE.does: Interactive tweed stack after the gain stages. Reissue owners call it very bright; Bass 0 / Mid 10 / Treble 0 is the flat point.

BASS.does: It generates a lot of bass and flubs when driven: run 0-3. First control to cut for 'tighter'.

MID.does: Fills the ~500 Hz scoop and raises level/drive into the power amp; crank it for a thicker, pushier tone.

PRESENCE.does: Power-amp negative-feedback treble boost: adds cut and edge after the preamp, most audible when the amp is loud.

model_notes.1123: Jumpered, plugged into the Bright channel: both volumes are live.
model_notes.1124: Bright channel alone. Whether VOLUME NORMAL still does anything is not documented.
model_notes.1125: Jumpered, plugged into the Normal channel: both volumes are live.
model_notes.1126: Normal channel alone: darker and fatter. Whether VOLUME BRIGHT still does anything is not documented.

boosts.why: Yek: 'for some vintage fun, put the Face Fuzz before the amp' - the amp's compression smooths it.
A treble booster controls the amp's heavy low end while pushing it into drive.
Bass cut plus mid hump tightens the loose tweed lows for leads.
Low-gain push for edge-of-breakup without thinning the tweed mids.

cabs.why: The Bassman's own open-back 4×10 with Jensen P10R alnicos.
Blonde Bassman cab with Vintage 30s: tighter, more mid-forward for rock.

known_for: 'Grandfather of rock and roll' amps; the circuit Marshall copied for the JTM45
Blues, rock'n'roll, rockabilly, roots: Buddy Guy, Brian Setzer, Eric Clapton, Jimi Hendrix
Clean, funk, soul through to raw overdrive
fender_tweed_bassman.poor_at: Tight palm-muted low end, glassy scooped cleans at volume, high gain.
fender_tweed_bassman.watch_out: With BASS near noon it farts out as soon as the volume goes up: start with BASS at 0-2 and add MID instead.

fender_tweed_twin_high_power.voice: Bassman-like but warmer, bigger and louder: dark, fat tweed clean with lots of headroom; compresses and fattens more than it distorts.

VOLUME NORMAL.does: Gain of the darker Normal channel; in Patch models it adds body. Keith Urban plugs into Normal.

VOLUME BRIGHT.does: Gain of the Bright channel. With single coils you must crank it to reach overdrive, and even then it mostly gets fatter.

TREBLE.does: Dark amp with its stock-style cab: run TREBLE higher than you would on a Bassman.

BASS.does: Turn it down; lots of lows from the tweed stack and 2×12 cabinet.

MID.does: Fills the scoop and adds push; Bonamassa-style settings run it nearly full.

PRESENCE.does: Power-amp feedback treble; turn it up along with TREBLE to open the dark voicing.

model_notes.1133: Jumpered, plugged into Normal: both volumes live.
model_notes.1135: Jumpered, plugged into Bright: both volumes live.

starts.name: Joe Bonamassa settings (converted from the 1-12 dials)

boosts.why: The amp barely overdrives on its own with single coils; a mid-hump drive supplies gain and tightens the lows.
Its TREBLE control lifts the dark voicing while adding a little grit.
Bass and treble controls let you brighten and tighten a dark, fat amp while adding gain.

cabs.why: Tweed Twin 2×12 with Weber Classic alnicos - the matching cab in the catalog.
Keith Urban's Twin cab had Two-Rock speakers that sound close to G12-65s (Yek).

known_for: Keith Richards, Eric Clapton, Rory Gallagher, Joe Bonamassa, Keith Urban
Loud fat tweed clean for blues, roots rock and country
fender_tweed_twin_high_power.poor_at: Bright sparkle or real distortion by itself; with single coils it barely overdrives.
fender_tweed_twin_high_power.watch_out: It sounds dark with its matching cab: do not judge it at noon - raise TREBLE and PRESENCE and cut BASS first.

vox_ac30.real: Vox AC30 (1959→; Top Boost early 1960s; QC panel matches the AC30 Hand-Wired), 30 W, 4×EL84 cathode-biased, no negative feedback, 2×12
vox_ac30.voice: Chime and jangle with a forward upper-mid bite; compressed, harmonically rich EL84 breakup; lows go loose when cranked.

VOLUME.does: Non-master preamp gain. Real amp: jangly clean around 11-12 o'clock (4-5), light crunch from 2-3 o'clock (7-8).

TONE CUT.does: INVERTED. Power-amp treble cut: up = darker/smoother, 0 = brightest. Use it to tame fizz instead of TREBLE.

TREBLE.does: Top Boost model. Very interactive: raising TREBLE also cuts BASS. Start both at 5.

BASS.does: Top Boost model. More lows but also a deeper mid notch as it rises; low BASS = tighter and more midrange.

BOOST.does: Top Boost model. Assumed = Hand-Wired HOT mode: partly bypasses TREBLE/BASS for much more gain and mids.

BRIGHT.does: Normal model. Adds high-end sparkle to the darker, EQ-less Normal channel.

model_notes.1009: Normal channel: no tone stack, darker with fuller mids - the 'Brian May' sound, made for a treble booster. Only BRIGHT and TONE CUT shape it.
model_notes.1011: Top Boost channel: Bass/Treble stack with a midrange cut - the classic chimey AC30.

boosts.why: The historic pairing: a treble booster adds gain and bite to the dark Normal channel and tightens the loose lows.
Boosting the input is the standard way to get more gain from a Vox; low-gain, keeps the chime.
Mid-hump drives suit the AC30's fixed-mid voicing and firm up the low end.

cabs.why: AC30 2×12 with Celestion alnico 'Silver Bell' drivers: the bright, chimey original voice.
AC30 with Greenbacks: warmer, woodier, less top - good when driven.
Open-back 2×12 with Alnico Golds: modern take on the alnico Vox voice with more headroom.

known_for: The Beatles and the British Invasion
Brian May (Queen), The Edge (U2), Rory Gallagher, Radiohead, Kings of Leon
Indie jangle and praise & worship edge-of-breakup tones
vox_ac30.poor_at: Tight low end and big clean headroom; scooped modern or high-gain tones. No feedback loop, so the lows loosen when cranked.
vox_ac30.watch_out: TONE CUT works backwards (up = darker). The scratchy top when driven is real: raise TONE CUT rather than killing TREBLE, which also shifts the bass and mids.

vox_ac15.real: Vox AC15 (1958→; Top Boost), 15 W, 2×EL84 cathode-biased, no negative feedback, 1×12
vox_ac15.voice: The AC30's little brother: same chime and upper-mid bite, but breaks up sooner with a softer, more compressed, smaller low end.

VOLUME.does: Non-master preamp gain; half the output tubes of an AC30, so the power amp gives up sooner.

TONE CUT.does: INVERTED. Power-amp treble cut: up = darker/smoother, 0 = brightest.

TREBLE.does: Top Boost model. Interactive: raising TREBLE also cuts BASS. Start both at 5.

BASS.does: Top Boost model. Adds lows and deepens the mid notch; keep low when driven.

BOOST.does: Top Boost model. Assumed = Hand-Wired HOT mode: partly bypasses the tone controls for more gain.

BRIGHT.does: Normal model. Adds top-end sparkle to the dark Normal channel.

model_notes.1127: Normal channel: no tone stack, darker and thicker; shape with BRIGHT, TONE CUT and a booster.
model_notes.1128: Top Boost channel: Bass/Treble stack and the classic chime.

boosts.why: Treble booster into an EL84 Vox: more gain and bite, less flub.
Input boost is the standard way to add gain to a Vox while keeping the chime.
Mid hump and bass cut firm up the small amp's loose low end.

cabs.why: The AC15's own 1×12 with a Celestion Alnico Blue.
Bigger 2×12 alnico Vox voice when the 1×12 sounds boxy.

known_for: The James Bond theme was recorded on an AC15
Studio-size Vox chime: British rock, indie, worship
Players listed for it: Brian May, The Edge, Rory Gallagher
vox_ac15.poor_at: Headroom and low-end authority; tight or scooped high-gain tones.
vox_ac15.watch_out: TONE CUT works backwards (up = darker), and it compresses early: for a cleaner sound lower VOLUME, do not just cut TREBLE.

marshall_jtm45.real: Marshall JTM45 (model 2245, 1962–66), 30–45 W, KT66/5881, GZ34 rectifier; derived from the 5F6-A Bassman
marshall_jtm45.drive_control: GAIN (the amp's volume; GAIN 1 / GAIN 2 on Patch)
marshall_jtm45.voice: Tweed-like Marshall: warm, saggy, round crunch with thick mids and soft attack; less bite and tightness than a Plexi.

GAIN.does: The channel volume (no master): drives preamp and power amp together. High settings turn low notes muddy and fuzzy.

GAIN 1.does: Patch model. By Marshall convention channel I = High Treble: brighter and gainier. Verify by ear.

GAIN 2.does: Patch model. By Marshall convention channel II = Normal: dark and bassy; adds body. Keep at or below GAIN 1.

BASS.does: Bass-heavy circuit: players run it at 0-3, often fully off, to stop flub and fuzz.

MID.does: Stack sits after the gain stages: MID up fills the scoop and pushes the power amp harder.

TREBLE.does: Dominant control of the interactive stack; crank the tone controls for a warm overdriven blues tone.

PRESENCE.does: Power-amp negative-feedback treble: adds cut and a rawer edge, most audible when the amp is driven.

model_notes.1038: Normal channel: dark, bassy, no bright cap; fat blues tones - turn BASS way down.
model_notes.1039: High Treble channel: very bright and also bass-heavy; closest to a Super Lead.
model_notes.1040: Jumpered channels with two gains; the Bluesbreaker-style blend.

boosts.why: Drive 0 / Level up trims the amp's heavy bass and pushes it into singing sustain (Gary Moore-style setting above).
1960s British pairing: a treble booster removes the flub and adds bite.
Mid-rich compressed Marshall-type amps smooth out fuzz pedals.
Clean-ish level push when you want the amp's own crunch at lower GAIN.

cabs.why: Late-60s Marshall 4×12 with G12M Greenbacks: the cab the amp was designed for.
Marshall 4×12 with Pulsonic Greenbacks: sweet mids, soft top.
Open-back 2×12 with pre-Rola Greenbacks: the closest thing here to a Bluesbreaker combo.
Marshall 4×12 with Alnico Creams: smoother, more touch-compressed vintage voice.

known_for: Eric Clapton on John Mayall's 'Beano' album (1966, Bluesbreaker combo)
British blues and blues-rock; Gary Moore-style leads
marshall_jtm45.poor_at: Tight, aggressive hard-rock crunch or metal: it has more sag and less crunch than later Marshalls and turns to mud with gain and bass up.
marshall_jtm45.watch_out: In the real world nobody ran the volume high; with GAIN way up low notes go muddy and almost synth-like. Stay moderate, BASS near 0, and boost from the front.

marshall_plexi_50.real: Marshall Lead 50, model 1987 (plexi panel 1966–69, then JMP; '50-watt Plexi'), 50 W, 2×EL34
marshall_plexi_50.drive_control: GAIN (the amp's volume; GAIN 1 / GAIN 2 on Patch)
marshall_plexi_50.voice: Plexi roar that gives up sooner: a little more aggressive and compressed than the 100, with easier power-amp crunch.

GAIN.does: The channel volume (no master): the amp relies on power-amp distortion, so real crunch needs it well up.

GAIN 1.does: Patch model. By Marshall convention channel I = High Treble (bright cap, more gain). Verify by ear.

GAIN 2.does: Patch model. By Marshall convention channel II = Normal: dark, loads of bass. Keep at or below GAIN 1.

BASS.does: Run it very low, even 0 - especially on Normal and Patch models - or the low end flubs.

MID.does: Post-gain stack: MID up fills the scoop and adds push; 7-10 is normal for a Plexi.

TREBLE.does: Do not be afraid to run it very high, as on the real amp; dominant control of the stack.

PRESENCE.does: Treble boost from reduced negative feedback in the power amp: cut, rasp and looser feel; set to taste.

model_notes.1079: High Treble (Bright) channel: bright cap makes it borderline painful at low GAIN, mellowing as GAIN rises; the gainiest single channel.
model_notes.1081: Normal channel: flat, dark, loads of bass; turn BASS way down.

starts.name: edge / cleans up with guitar volume (Bright)

boosts.why: Treble booster into a cranked Marshall: tightens the lows and adds singing gain.
The amp's compression smooths a Fuzz Face into the creamy 60s lead sound.
Level-up, gain-low boost trims bass and adds saturation for tighter leads; can turn boxy since the amp is already mid-rich.
Scooped Big Muff-type fuzz suits mid-rich, compressed British amps.

cabs.why: Marshall 4×12 with Pulsonic G12M Greenbacks: sweet mids, the period-correct pairing.
1969 tall 4×12 with G12M-25s: bigger low end, vintage top.
G12H30s: compress less than Greenbacks and are flatter - the 'Hendrix speaker' type.

known_for: Classic rock and hard rock crunch; the smaller sibling of the Super Lead
Players of Plexis generally: Hendrix, Page, Angus Young, Van Halen
marshall_plexi_50.poor_at: Clean headroom, tight modern low end and smooth highs: raspy by design and non-master, so it only sings when driven.
marshall_plexi_50.watch_out: Do not dial it like a master-volume amp: BASS at noon = flub. Run BASS 0-3 with MID and TREBLE high; the fizz on top is how a Plexi sounds.

marshall_plexi_100.real: Marshall Super Lead 100, model 1959 (1965→; plexi panel to 1969), 100 W, 4×EL34
marshall_plexi_100.drive_control: GAIN (the amp's volume; GAIN 1 / GAIN 2 on Patch)
marshall_plexi_100.voice: The classic-rock roar: bright, raspy, open and huge with upper-mid 'kerrang'; more headroom and punch than the 50.

GAIN.does: The channel volume (no master): power-amp distortion does the work; back the guitar volume off for a warm clean.

GAIN 1.does: Patch model. By Marshall convention channel I = High Treble (bright cap, more gain). Verify by ear.

GAIN 2.does: Patch model. By Marshall convention channel II = Normal: dark, loads of bass. Keep at or below GAIN 1.

BASS.does: Run it very low, even 0, or it gets flubby - most of all on the Normal channel.

MID.does: Post-gain stack: MID up fills the scoop and adds push; 8-10 is normal.

TREBLE.does: Run it high without fear, as on the real amp; dominant control of the stack.

PRESENCE.does: Treble boost from reduced negative feedback in the power amp; set to taste (JD Simo: 5-6).

model_notes.1091: High Treble (Bright) channel: boosted bright tone bordering on painful; its bright cap is also part of its gain.
model_notes.1093: Normal channel: flat response, dark, loads of bass.

starts.name: edge / cleans up with guitar volume (Bright)

boosts.why: The Hendrix recipe: the Plexi's compression smooths a Fuzz Face into a creamy lead.
Treble booster into a loud Marshall: tighter lows and more singing gain.
Level-up, gain-low boost trims bass and adds saturation for tighter leads; can turn boxy since the amp is already mid-rich.
Scooped Big Muff-type fuzz suits mid-rich, compressed British amps.

cabs.why: Marshall 4×12 with Pulsonic G12M Greenbacks: the stack sound.
1969 tall cab with G12M-25s: big lows, sweet vintage top.
G12H30s compress less and are flatter than Greenbacks - the 'Hendrix speaker' type.
Angled 1960A with G12M-25s: slightly more modern Greenback voice.

known_for: Jimi Hendrix, Jimmy Page, Pete Townshend, Angus Young, Eddie Van Halen (everything on…
The sound of classic and hard rock; the Marshall stack
marshall_plexi_100.poor_at: Clean headroom at the settings where it sounds best, tight modern low end, smooth highs; raspy and fizzy by design.
marshall_plexi_100.watch_out: Do not dial it like a master-volume amp: BASS at noon = flub. Run BASS 0-3 with MID/TREBLE high. Turning the bright channel down in gain also makes it thinner and harsher.

hiwatt_dr103.real: Hiwatt Custom 100 DR103 (late 1960s→; Harry Joyce-era 1970s), 100 W, 4×EL34
hiwatt_dr103.voice: Loud, hi-fi British clean: tight punchy lows, strong forward mids, glassy slightly hollow top; stiff, with crunch only when cranked.

GAIN.does: Channel volume. Gilmour keeps it around 2 o'clock (7) with a low master for a thick clean on the edge.

MASTER.does: Real master volume. Low = clean, tight pedal platform; crank it with GAIN for raw power-amp roar.

BASS.does: Wide-range and effective (unlike a Plexi's). Gilmour settings range from 2.5 to 8 depending on cab and era.

MID.does: Adds strong punch; the amp is already mid-forward. Gilmour settings span roughly 3 to 8.

TREBLE.does: Wide-range; Gilmour usually keeps it low (2-4) and gets clarity from PRESENCE.

PRESENCE.does: Subtle power-amp control: 'doesn't do a lot but it opens up the amp a little'.

model_notes.1063: Normal channel: voiced to stay clean and powerful at all levels; fuller and darker.
model_notes.1064: Brilliant channel: higher gain and brighter; the one that overdrives when pushed.

starts.name: Gilmour 2006 'On an Island' tour (clock positions converted)

boosts.why: Gilmour's Big Muff sound depends on a mid-rich, compressed Hiwatt to fill in and smooth the scooped fuzz.
Fuzz Face-type pedals turn smooth and creamy into darker British amps like a Hiwatt.
Flat/transparent boosts suit an amp that already has plenty of mids (the Powerboost role).

cabs.why: Hiwatt's own SE4123 4×12 - Hiwatt and Fane speakers go hand in hand.
Gilmour has also run a Marshall 4×12 alongside his WEM cab.

known_for: David Gilmour / Pink Floyd clean platform for fuzz and delay
Pete Townshend / The Who - 'Live at Leeds'
Players listed for it: Kevin Shields, Robert Fripp
hiwatt_dr103.poor_at: Easy low-volume breakup or saggy vintage feel: it is stiff and clean. Mid-hump drives (Green 808, Rodent Drive, Obsessive Drive) can sound dark and boxy into it.
hiwatt_dr103.watch_out: Do not expect a Plexi: at normal settings it stays clean. Use it as a loud clean base (GAIN ~7, MASTER low) and get the drive from a fuzz or flat overdrive in front.

roland_jc120.real: Roland JC-120 Jazz Chorus (1975→), solid-state, 2×60 W stereo, 2×12
roland_jc120.drive_control: none (VOLUME is level; the amp stays clean)
roland_jc120.voice: Pristine, open, fast solid-state clean: tight lows, glassy bright top, no sag or compression; the 80s chorus clean.

VOLUME.does: Level only - no tube-style breakup to dial in. The real amp's built-in distortion is not modeled.

BRIGHT.does: Roland manual: ON gives 'a bright, clear sound'. Yek always engages it; switch off if the top is harsh.

BASS.does: Conventional bass control; the amp is already tight, so cut only to make room in a mix.

MID.does: Conventional mid control; dip slightly for the glassy 80s clean, raise for body with pedals.

TREBLE.does: Conventional treble control on a naturally bright amp; back it off before blaming a drive pedal for harshness.

model_notes.1008: Amp section only: the famous stereo chorus is not in the amp block - put Chief CE2W (ST) after the amp/cab to recreate it in stereo.

boosts.why: Yek: great overdriven tones from a JC-120 with a Tube Screamer; it adds the mids and compression the amp never will.
Full distortion pedals supply all the dirt; Rat-type mids and compression suit a flat, uncompressed clean amp.
Amp-like overdrive with fat lows and strong mids for a clean amp with no breakup of its own.

cabs.why: The JC-120's own 2×12.

known_for: Andy Summers (The Police), Robert Smith, Johnny Marr - 80s chorus cleans
Metallica clean parts ('Fade to Black', 'Welcome Home (Sanitarium)', 'Nothing Else…
roland_jc120.poor_at: Any amp breakup, warmth, sag or touch compression; cannot do 'edge of breakup' by itself.
roland_jc120.watch_out: It never 'gives': with no compression, pick attack and harsh pedal top-end come through raw. Add a compressor and take all dirt from pedals with their tone rolled back.

matchless_chieftain.real: Matchless Chieftain (1990s→), 40 W, 2×EL34 cathode-biased class A, no negative feedback, tube rectifier
matchless_chieftain.voice: Thick yet crisp boutique EL34 tone: fat lows, rich complex mids, shimmering top; fair power-amp breakup, very touch-sensitive.

VOLUME.does: First-stage gain: sensitivity and drive. Cleans up well from the guitar's volume when set for overdrive.

BASS.does: Very wide range; too much causes floppiness and loss of definition at high volume (manual). Keep it low.

MID.does: Interactive with BASS and TREBLE; adds body and push.

TREBLE.does: Per the manual it regulates the mid-band and upper mids (the instrument's 'voice'), not just the extreme top.

BRILLIANCE.does: Power-amp high-frequency control: smooths or brings forward the top edge. Reported as up = brighter (unverified).

MASTER.does: Output-amp gain. Maximum = most clean headroom and power-amp feel; lower it and raise VOLUME for dirtier preamp tone.

boosts.why: Low-gain push into an amp that already has rich mids and its own power-amp breakup.
Clean boost with bass/treble trim: more drive without adding the bass the amp punishes.
Bass cut and mid focus tighten the wide, soft low end for leads.

cabs.why: The Chieftain's own 2×12 with Matchless signature drivers.
Chieftain cab with Vintage 30s: more upper-mid cut, tighter.

known_for: Roots and alternative rock; Matchless players such as David Grissom and Kings of Leon
matchless_chieftain.poor_at: Tight high-gain or scooped tones; the low end flops if BASS is up at volume.
matchless_chieftain.watch_out: The BASS knob has far more range than usual: 'more bass' quickly becomes floppy and undefined. Also check BRILLIANCE direction by ear before automating it.

matchless_dc30.real: Matchless DC-30 (C-30 series; Matchless's first design, c. 1989–91→), 30 W, 4×EL84 cathode-biased class A, no negative feedback; Ch1 12AX7, Ch2 EF86
matchless_dc30.voice: A sturdier, hi-fi AC30: chime, shimmer and crunch with more clarity and firmer lows; Ch2 (EF86) is thicker and gainier.

VOLUME.does: Preamp gain; very input-sensitive - dig in and it compresses and gets juicy.

BASS.does: Ch1. Top-Boost-style active stack: BASS and TREBLE are highly interactive.

TREBLE.does: Ch1. Interactive with BASS; the classic chime control.

CUT.does: INVERTED like a Vox cut: power-amp treble cut, up = darker. Subtle below half, strong above; works best with MASTER high.

MASTER.does: Bypassable on the real amp; full up is the open, power-amp-driven tone. Lower it for preamp drive at less level.

TONE.does: Ch2. Six-position switch on the real amp: lowest = thinnest, each step up = thicker. Not a treble knob.

model_notes.1155: Channel 1: two 12AX7s, AC30 Top Boost-type voice; chime and jangle to crunch. The favourite for clean-with-chime.
model_notes.1156: Channel 2: EF86 pentode, more gain and overdrives harder; the 'heavier' channel, shaped by the thickness TONE switch.

boosts.why: Input boost keeps the chime while adding grit - the usual way to push AC-style amps.
Treble booster into EL84 class-A: more bite and gain, firmer lows.
Mid hump and bass cut for tighter leads from a loose, chimey amp.

cabs.why: The DC-30's own 2×12 (the real combo pairs a modified G12H30 with a Greenback).
Second capture of the same cabinet; pick the one that sits better.

known_for: 'An AC30 that wouldn't break down' - studio and touring workhorse
Nashville session players; country, roots, indie
The amp that started the boutique craze
matchless_dc30.poor_at: Scooped or high-gain tones and big clean headroom at volume.

morgan_sw50.real: Morgan SW50 (2010s; built around a ~40-year-old Dumble-style clean amp, widely linked to the Steel String Singer), 50 W, 2×6L6
morgan_sw50.drive_control: MASTER (the amp's Level = power-section gain) with GAIN
morgan_sw50.voice: Mid-60s blackface idea with more clarity and string-to-string definition: loud, big clean with sweet singing sustain.

BRIGHT.does: Brings in top end for dark guitars 'without adding any ice picky highs'.

LOW BOOST.does: Morgan's bass-emphasis switch: moves the mid centre point so more bass comes through. Off for tighter.

GAIN.does: Preamp volume (assumed mapping). Keep moderate for maximum clean headroom.

BASS.does: Interacts with TREBLE for a wide tonal range.

MID.does: Midrange body; more mid than a blackface stack offers.

TREBLE.does: Interacts with BASS for a wide tonal range.

MASTER.does: The amp's Level: power-section gain. Past ~3 o'clock (8) it adds warm, compressed power-amp overdrive.

Fat amp-like drive for when the platform has to cover crunch.

EVM12L: maximum headroom, firm lows and clarity for a clean platform.

known_for: Players listed for it: Josh Smith, Tosin Abasi, Aaron Marshall
morgan_sw50.poor_at: Amp distortion: only mild power-amp grit at high MASTER; needs pedals for crunch and lead.
morgan_sw50.watch_out: Roles are swapped compared with most amps: the overdrive comes from MASTER (Level), not GAIN. Re-check loudness with OUTPUT after moving MASTER.

dumble_ods.real: Dumble Overdrive Special (QC: a 1992 'low-plate Skyliner, non-HRM' amp), 6L6; OD channel cascades from the clean preamp
dumble_ods.drive_control: VOLUME (clean gain, also feeds the OD) and OD CONTENT on the OD channel
dumble_ods.voice: Fenderish fat clean with strong low-mids; OD channel is thick, mid-heavy, smooth and vocal - sings on single notes, very touch-sensitive.

CHANNEL.does: Clean / OD. The OD stages come after the clean preamp, so VOLUME and the tone stack still shape the OD.

VOLUME.does: Clean-preamp gain. As it rises the tone moves from sparkly upper-mid emphasis to thick, bassy and meaty.

TREBLE.does: Shared stack placed before the OD stages: on the OD channel it works as pre-distortion EQ.

MIDDLE.does: Shared pre-OD stack; more MIDDLE = more signal and thicker drive.

BASS.does: Shared pre-OD stack: bass here goes into the overdrive, so high settings make the OD muddy.

OD CONTENT.does: Amount of OD-channel saturation (forum: 'controls the preamp saturation'); barely changes the tonal balance.

OD VOLUME.does: OD-channel level: balances OD against clean at the same MASTER setting.

MASTER.does: Power-amp level and feel. Users report clean much quieter than OD (MASTER 8-9 to match OD VOLUME 5).

PRESENCE.does: Power-amp top end.

PREAMP.does: Assumed = preamp boost (PAB): bypasses the tone stack for more gain and mids; the EQ knobs then do little.

BRIGHT.does: Adds sparkle; less noticeable as VOLUME goes up. Forum tip: off for single coils, on for humbuckers.

MID.does: Mid boost (a.k.a. Deep): more mids and gain, fatter. Forum tip: on for single coils, off for humbuckers.

EQ.does: Rock / Jazz. Rock is brighter, stronger, more dynamic; Jazz adds low-pass filtering: softer, rounder, lower gain.

boosts.why: Into the clean channel: mid focus and bass cut keep the cascaded OD from getting woolly.
Low-gain push on the clean channel for edge-of-breakup while leaving the OD channel for leads.
Bass and treble controls let you trim what goes into an amp whose EQ sits before its overdrive.

known_for: Robben Ford, Larry Carlton, Carlos Santana, Eric Johnson, John Mayer, Joe Bonamassa,…

dumble_ods.watch_out: The OD is cascaded: clean VOLUME and BASS decide how muddy it gets. Keep BASS low and VOLUME moderate, and expect a big clean/OD level gap to fix with OD VOLUME.

mesa_lone_star.real: Mesa/Boogie Lone Star (original 'Classic', introduced mid-2000s), 100/50 W switchable, 4×6L6, built-in variac 'Tweed' power mode
mesa_lone_star.drive_control: GAIN (clean models); DRIVE with GAIN (drive models)
mesa_lone_star.voice: Polished blackface-style clean with rounder, fatter low-mids and big headroom; Drive channel is smooth, thick and singing.

GAIN.does: Gain AND tone: low (0-4) bright and 3-D, middle (4-7) warmer and fuller - the sweet spot, high = saturated lows, soft attack.

TREBLE.does: Dominant control, first in the stack: high TREBLE starves MID and BASS and adds gain. Sweet spot about 4-6.5.

MID.does: Low (0-4) = scooped, girthy, softer feel; 4.5-6.5 fills in with focused attack; higher = stiffer, more forward, more gain.

PRESENCE.does: High-cut at the END OF THE PREAMP (not power-amp feedback): lower = darker and more compressed, fat for leads.

MASTER.does: Channel master; Mesa suggests staying in its sensible range (about 2-7).

model_notes.1104: Clean, 100 W, Tweed: big but softer and scoopier.

model_notes.1106: Drive, 50 W, Tweed: loosest, most vintage-feeling lead.
model_notes.1107: Drive, 100 W, normal power: tightest, boldest lead of the four.
model_notes.1108: Drive, 100 W, Tweed: big lead with a spongier attack.

bogner_shiva_clean.real: Bogner Shiva 20th Anniversary (KT88, 90 W) - clean channel
bogner_shiva_clean.voice: Beefy, warm, slightly dark clean with big KT88 headroom; shimmers once Treble, Bright and Presence come up; crunch only near the top.

BRIGHT.does: Bright switch; less effective the higher GAIN is set.

BASS.does: Bass of the clean stack; the tone controls stay in circuit on the 20th Anniversary.

model_notes.1117: KT88 version has less gain and more headroom than EL34 Shivas. The real amp's clean Boost is not exposed as a parameter.

boosts.why: High-headroom clean takes a low-gain mid push well; its TREBLE control offsets the dark voicing.

friedman_be100_clean.real: Friedman BE-100 (HBE100) - clean channel; 100 W, 4×EL34, modded-Plexi lineage
friedman_be100_clean.voice: Chimey Plexi-style clean: brighter, firmer and more mid-present than a blackface Fender, with EL34 snap and little scoop.

BRIGHT.does: Three-position switch that varies the overall brightness of the clean channel only; choose by ear.

TREBLE.does: Clean-channel treble. Manual start: 5.

VOLUME.does: The clean channel's only level control (no separate master): turn up to taste; high settings add grit.

model_notes.1027: The utility clean of a high-gain rock amp; the BE and HBE channels (1028, 1082) belong to the high-gain research set.

Mid-focused overdrive on a firm, bright clean for classic-rock leads.

marshall_jcm800.real: Marshall JCM800 2203 (100 W master-volume head, 1981 on)

1.signature: Clean path blended with Ge hard-clipped path; gain peaks ~1 kHz (mid hump); treble shelf from ~408 Hz (+18/-8 dB); 18 V rail headroom.

GAIN.does: Dual-gang pot: raises the clipped signal while lowering the clean feed-forward blend, so low GAIN is mostly clean boost.

TREBLE.does: Active high shelf above ~400 Hz, about +18 dB to -8 dB; noon is roughly flat.

LEVEL.does: Output volume (labelled OUTPUT on the pedal); the main control when used as a boost.

1.watch_out: Designed to work with an amp's own overdrive, not as the only dirt on a sterile clean amp; it cuts far less bass than a TS, so it tightens high-gain amps less.

2.signature: MOSFET clipping, amp-like and full-range with big low end; PEAK HP adds drive, bottom and upper mids, LP stays closer to guitar/amp tone.

PEAK.does: HP/LP = High Peak/Low Peak (not high-pass/low-pass). HP: more drive, volume, bottom and upper-mid emphasis. LP: flatter, closer to the bypassed tone.

TONE.does: Treble roll-off; one source says the PEAK switch also moves its shelving frequency.

DRIVE.does: Gain; wide range from clean-ish push to distortion.

2.watch_out: Full low end and high output: as a boost into a high-gain amp it adds bass and flub instead of tightening; HP mode is a volume jump versus LP.

3.signature: Op-amp gain into diodes to ground, no tone control; in the near-identical Distortion+ the bass corner climbs to ~720 Hz at max gain.

GAIN.does: Op-amp gain; raising it also raises the bass roll-off corner (3 Hz at minimum to ~720 Hz at maximum in the sister MXR Distortion+ circuit), so more gain = thinner lows.

VOLUME.does: Output level; high output makes it a strong amp pusher.

3.watch_out: No tone control and the lows thin out as GAIN rises; raspy into bright clean amps. Circuit numbers come from the MXR Distortion+ analysis (the 250 differs mainly in silicon diodes and a few values).

4.signature: Op-amp gain to 67 dB, lows below ~1.5 kHz get less gain, Si hard clip, slow LM308 softens highs; FILTER low-pass 475 Hz-32 kHz.

FILTER.does: Passive low-pass after clipping, cutoff ~32 kHz down to ~475 Hz. WORKS BACKWARDS: turning up cuts treble.

DISTORTION.does: Gain 0 to ~67 dB; low = overdrive, above about two-thirds = thick fuzz-like saturation.

VOLUME.does: Passive output level.

4.watch_out: FILTER is reversed versus every other tone knob (up = darker); any software 'brighter' move must decrease it. Fully up it is extremely dark.

5.signature: Lows below 720 Hz get less gain, 723 Hz low-pass after clipping: mid hump around 720 Hz; soft symmetric clip, gain 12x-118x.

OVERDRIVE.does: Clipping-stage gain 12x to 118x (41 dB); even at 0 the pedal still has gain and its bass cut/mid hump.

TONE.does: Active treble control after a fixed 723 Hz low-pass; at maximum it restores highs above ~3.2 kHz, at minimum it removes treble.

LEVEL.does: Output volume; the control that pushes the amp when used as a boost.

5.watch_out: Cuts lows and adds 700-800 Hz honk: thin and nasal alone into a clean amp, and too much midrange on an amp that is already mid-heavy or tight.

6.signature: RC Booster core plus clipping diodes and fixed TS-style mid voicing; active bass/treble boost-cut; most gain of the Xotic trio.

BASS.does: Active (Baxandall) low boost/cut; 5 is flat.

TREBLE.does: Active (Baxandall) high boost/cut; 5 is flat.

GAIN.does: Slightly dirty to heavily overdriven; compresses as it rises.

6.watch_out: BASS above noon into a dirty amp adds flub; the EQ is boost/cut, so 'neutral' is 5, not 0.

8.signature: Friedman BE-style cascaded high-gain preamp distortion; TIGHT cuts bass before clipping; bass/treble/presence EQ; very high output.

TIGHT.does: Bass cut at the first gain stage, before clipping; up = tighter, less low end into the distortion (forum reading of the schematic).

TRIM.does: Model of the pedal's internal gain trimmer: sets the overall gain range, from vintage-ish to extreme. Owners report running it low (about 8:30-9 o'clock).

PRESENCE.does: Upper-treble cut-through; raise for clarity in a band mix.

BASS.does: Post-distortion low end; interacts with TIGHT.

8.watch_out: It is a complete high-gain preamp: into an already distorted amp it becomes noisy, fizzy and over-compressed. Keep TRIM and GAIN low and gate it.

9.signature: Low-gain op-amp soft clipping with an open, un-humped midrange and a low gain ceiling; drive comes on gradually.

GAIN.does: Low overall range; even high settings stay in light-overdrive territory.

TONE.does: Single treble control (no 3-band EQ like the Guv'nor).

9.watch_out: Low gain and no real bass cut: it will not tighten a high-gain amp and cannot reshape mids.

10.signature: Transistor booster (35 dB) + op-amp (to 26.5 dB) into Si hard clip; Muff-style tone tilts LP 234 Hz / HP 1063 Hz around a ~500 Hz scoop.

TONE.does: Blends a 234 Hz low-pass against a 1063 Hz high-pass; mids are scooped around 500 Hz at noon. Up = treble side.

DISTORTION.does: Op-amp gain 0 to 26.5 dB on top of a fixed transistor boost; bass corner rises to ~72 Hz at maximum.

LEVEL.does: Output; the circuit loses level internally, so it usually sits well above noon.

10.watch_out: Scooped around 500 Hz and fizzy above noon TONE, so it can vanish in a band mix into a clean amp; it is the opposite EQ shape to a Tube Screamer.

11.signature: LED hard clipping (~1.8-2 V, high headroom), ~70 dB total gain, 723 Hz pre-clip high-pass, Marshall-style interactive 3-band stack.

MID.does: FMV-style stack: almost every setting leaves a scoop between 1 and 3 kHz, so MID usually needs to be up.

BASS.does: Passive, interactive with MID and TREBLE.

TREBLE.does: Passive, interactive.

11.watch_out: The tone stack is interactive and scooped by default; in front of an already Marshall-voiced dirty amp the voicing doubles up and turns harsh.

12.signature: Dual-stage high gain with seven filters pre/post; active LOW/HIGH +/-15 dB and a +/-15 dB MIDDLE sweepable 200 Hz-5 kHz.

MIDFREQ.does: Sweeps the MIDDLE band from 200 Hz to 5 kHz; behaves almost like a global voicing control.

HIGH.does: Active shelving +/-15 dB; rolling back removes fizz but too far removes upper mids.

12.watch_out: EQ range is +/-15 dB, so move in small steps from 5; maxed DIST and HIGH is the notorious 'buzzing bees' tone. Start with lower gain than seems necessary.

13.signature: The original asymmetric soft-clipping overdrive (ancestor of TS and SD-1); no tone control; more bass roll-off than the SD-1.

GAIN.does: Overdrive amount; no tone control exists, so voicing is fixed.

13.watch_out: No tone control: if the boosted tone is too dark or too nasal the only fix is amp EQ or another pedal.

14.signature: Asymmetric soft clipping (2 diodes one side, 1 the other); midrange focus ~800 Hz; less bass roll-off than OD-1/TS, so fuller.

TONE.does: Treble control added over the OD-1.

OVERDRIVE.does: Gain; set high it adds grit in front of an already-overdriven amp.

14.watch_out: Fuller lows than a Tube Screamer, so on an already boomy amp it tightens less.

15.signature: Booster + two cascaded diode-clipping stages; tone blends LP/HP around a ~1 kHz notch (about -13.5 dB total at noon); huge sustain.

TONE.does: Single pot blending a low-pass and a high-pass: down = bass side, up = treble side, mids scooped around 1 kHz in the middle. It can never be flat.

SUSTAIN.does: Level into the clipping stages (gain); high settings hold saturation even from a weak signal.

15.watch_out: Scooped at ~1 kHz, so it disappears in a band mix; into a distorted amp it turns to mush. Pair it with a mid-forward stage (e.g. a TS) rather than more gain.

18.signature: Bright, full-range, touch-sensitive overdrive without a pronounced mid hump; cleans up with picking and guitar volume (community consensus).

GAIN.does: Clean-ish boost at low settings through crunchy overdrive.

18.watch_out: No circuit source was fetched for this model; the usual complaint is brightness/harshness with TONE above noon into a bright amp.

21.signature: Single germanium transistor, up to 38 dB gain; 5 nF input cap high-passes at ~2.6 kHz so only treble gets full gain; soft clipping.

VOLUME.does: The only control: amount of boost (and, near maximum, soft clipping). There is no tone control; the treble emphasis is fixed.

21.watch_out: Built to cut the mud from a dark, already-overdriven tube amp; into a clean or bright amp it is thin and shrill. Low input impedance (~10-12 k) means it belongs first in the chain.

22.signature: Two-transistor feedback fuzz; very low input impedance (~5-8 kOhm) loads the pickups, which is why guitar volume cleans it up.

FUZZ.does: Sets second-stage emitter degeneration/feedback: more = more gain and harder clipping. Conventionally run at or near maximum, with the guitar volume used to clean up.

VOLUME.does: Output level; the real circuit has little output gain and lower settings thin the bass.

PICKUP.does: Not documented by Neural DSP. Presumably a pickup-loading simulation for the low-impedance input (unverified).

PICKUP LEVEL.does: Not documented by Neural DSP (unverified; possibly the simulated guitar-volume/pickup level feeding the fuzz).

22.watch_out: Must be first: a buffer, wah or any pedal in front changes it for the worse (low input impedance). PICKUP / PICKUP LEVEL are undocumented, so software should leave them at defaults.

23.signature: Clean boost / low-gain preamp with active bass and treble; 'clean to slightly dirty'; BB Preamp core without the clipping diodes.

BASS.does: Active low boost/cut; 5 is flat. Cut it to tighten.

TREBLE.does: Active high boost/cut; 5 is flat.

GAIN.does: Clean to slightly dirty.

23.watch_out: Flat and full-range: it only tightens a high-gain amp if BASS is turned down; BASS above noon adds flub.

24.signature: Modded TS9-family overdrive with a FET input stage and Lo/Hi gain modes; TS mid voicing with more range.

MODE.does: Lo/Hi gain. Lo: thicker with more midrange. Hi: fatter with more gain range.

24.watch_out: Same family caveats as a Tube Screamer (bass cut, mid honk); Hi mode in front of a high-gain amp adds gain and noise rather than tightness.

25.signature: Low/medium-gain transparent overdrive voiced after blackface Fender 'Magic 6' tones; less compression and colour than a TS.

BASS.does: Low-frequency control (direction on the model not verified).

TREBLE.does: High-frequency control (direction on the model not verified).

GAIN.does: Light breakup to medium overdrive with natural-feeling compression.

25.watch_out: Low gain and uncompressed, so not a high-gain tightener; the real pedal's saturation trimmer is not exposed in the QC parameters.

26.signature: 'The other green overdrive': balanced EQ without the TS mid spike and bass cut; SPECTRUM raises highs and lower-mids together.

SPECTRUM.does: Dual filter, not a simple tone knob: turning up boosts highs AND lower-mids at once; turning down cuts both, leaving a more midrange-forward sound.

BASS CUT.does: Trims the low end, which is otherwise prominent with humbuckers (added on later ODR-1 versions).

MUTE TRIG.does: Internal trigger parameter; leave at default.

26.watch_out: Full low end: without BASS CUT it gets boomy with humbuckers or in front of a dirty amp. SPECTRUM changes two bands at once.

27.signature: Second catalog entry with the same name and parameters as id 5: bass cut below 720 Hz, mid hump ~720 Hz, soft clip.

OVERDRIVE.does: Clipping-stage gain 12x to 118x; still coloured at 0.

TONE.does: Active treble control after a fixed 723 Hz low-pass.

27.watch_out: Duplicate of id 5 in the catalog (which one is current is not documented); same honk/thin-lows caveats.

28.signature: High-gain distortion with active bass and treble cut/boost and a wide gain range (very little to a lot).

BASS.does: Active low cut/boost; start at 5.

TREBLE.does: Active high cut/boost; start at 5.

USE GATE.does: QC-side gate switch; the hardware pedal's documentation found does not mention a gate.

28.watch_out: A distortion, not a boost: stacking it into a dirty amp multiplies noise. EQ is active boost/cut, so 5 is neutral.

29.signature: Silicon take on the 1973 Sola Sound Tone Bender MKIII: three-transistor-style fuzz with a tone sweep; smoother and thicker than a Fuzz Face.

ATTACK.does: The fuzz/distortion amount; more = more fuzz.

TONE.does: Sweeps between dark and bright (which direction is brighter was not verified).

29.watch_out: TONE direction unverified; the hardware's 'JHS mode' (more gain plus mid boost) is not exposed. Treat like any fuzz: early in the chain, clean-ish amp.

30.signature: Plugin boost/overdrive 'for tighter rhythms and saturated lead'; MODE switches Overdrive to Fuzz for richer harmonic distortion.
30.watch_out: No real pedal is named by Neural DSP. Fuzz mode adds harmonic distortion and is not a tightening boost.

32.signature: Neural: 'a modded classic; a booster loved by tube amp fanatics' (name implies a modded Tube Screamer-style circuit; not stated).

32.watch_out: Resemblance to a real pedal is inferred from the name only; BASS is undocumented.

33.signature: Neural: 'a heavy and powerful overdrive pedal that pushes saturation to the beginnings of fuzz'.
33.watch_out: No real pedal named. Heavy saturation into a clean funk amp can swamp note definition; keep DRIVE moderate.

34.signature: Second 'overdrive/booster' in Archetype: Nolly with gain, bass and treble; a reviewer calls it thicker and beefier, for adding dirt.

BASS.does: Low-frequency control.

TREBLE.does: High-frequency control.

35.signature: First 'overdrive/booster' in Archetype: Nolly; a reviewer calls it the usual green overdrive for tightening; adds a BRIGHT switch.

36.signature: Plugin 'Distortion pedal' with DIST / FILTER / VOL, the RAT control layout; FILTER is a low-pass that darkens as it is raised.

36.watch_out: FILTER is reversed (up = darker), like the RAT. Neural DSP does not name a real pedal; the RAT resemblance is by control layout only.

37.signature: Plugin 'Overdrive pedal (OD)' with DIST / TONE / LEVEL, placed before the amps for boosting.
37.watch_out: No real pedal or frequency behaviour is documented, so the amount of low cut is unknown; verify tightness by ear or measurement.

38.signature: The 'overdrive (OD2)' of the Soldano suite; HI PEAK switch adds a hi-mid frequency boost.

38.watch_out: No real pedal named. HI PEAK plus a bright SLO channel can get harsh in the upper mids.

39.signature: The 'boost (OD1)' of the Soldano suite: drive/tone/level booster ahead of the amp.

BASS.does: Low-end control present on the QC model; not described in the plugin manual v1.0.0.

39.watch_out: No real pedal named and BASS is undocumented; do not assume TS-style low cut.

40.signature: One-knob boost (marketed up to +20 dB) with fixed bass cut and upper-mid focus; 'adds clarity and articulation' ahead of high gain.

40.watch_out: Cuts a lot of bass and is a character pedal, not a transparent boost; a hobbyist measurement found far less than the claimed +20 dB, so set BOOST by output level, not by a dB assumption.

41.signature: Neural: 'an overdrive pedal with a higher output than most, with additional headroom and an irregular style of clipping'.

BASS.does: Low-end control present on the QC model; not described in the plugin manual v1.0.0.

41.watch_out: Higher output than most overdrives: LEVEL values that suit a TS will hit the amp harder here. BASS is undocumented.

42.signature: RAT-derived (1985 Whiteface starting point) drive with a fixed-level preamp and far less gain than a RAT; CUT is a treble-cut control.

CUT.does: Treble cut: the further up, the more highs are removed. WORKS BACKWARDS. Interacts with DRV (acts differently at low and high gain).

LEVEL.does: The pedal's volume knob, in percent.

OUTPUT.does: QC block output trim in dB (-60..12); not a pedal control. Keep at 0 dB unless level-matching.

42.watch_out: CUT is reversed (up = darker) and this is the only drive whose knobs are in percent with a separate dB OUTPUT; scale-sensitive code must special-case it.

43.signature: Plugin overdrive pedal (tone/drive/level) ahead of the Petrucci amps; no real pedal or voicing documented.

MODE.does: Present on the QC model; not described in the plugin manual v1.0.0.

43.watch_out: MODE is undocumented; leave it at default. Voicing unknown, so do not assume TS-style bass cut.

GAIN.does: Signal level feeding the overdrive.

48.signature: Two circuits: vintage mode is a mid-focused overdrive; modern mode is 'more transparent and dynamic'; bass/treble EQ.

49.signature: Custom DIY pedal inspired by a classic Swedish-metal distortion (HM-2 'chainsaw' style), made to front high-gain amps; clean blend.

50.signature: 'Inspired by a well-known green pedal, modified for use as a boost with high-gain amps'; ATTACK sets low-end cut; built-in gate.

BRIGHT.does: Brightness; turn up until the tone cuts. Intentionally strong and can get harsh at the top of its range on mid/low-gain tones.

GATE.does: Sensitivity of the built-in noise gate; 0 = gate fully bypassed. Low just removes noise; high gives a very tight, choppy stop.

50.watch_out: ATTACK is a rotary switch, not a 0..10 knob; BRIGHT and ATTACK are set by ear after DRIVE/VOLUME. Cranked GATE chokes sustain; reviewers note fizzy edges when pushed.

recipes.documented_gear: Style reference, not one artist: the traditional sound is a neck humbucker on a hollow archtop with heavy/flatwound strings into a clean, loud amp. No single documented rig is claimed here.

chain.why: Evens single-note lines without audible squash; many players use none.

chain.choice: clean high-headroom amp (blackface Fender Twin/Deluxe type or Roland JC type)
chain.settings: gain low, bass 3-4, mid 6-7, treble 3-4, bright off
chain.why: Fully clean with strong mids and restrained treble; bass kept low because the neck humbucker supplies it.
Open-back combos give the round, less directional low end.

chain.choice: ribbon or dynamic placed off the cap
chain.settings: toward the cone edge, 1-3 in back
chain.why: Avoids close-mic bite.

chain.settings: low cut 80 Hz; high cut 4-5 kHz; -2 dB at 200-250 Hz if boomy
chain.why: Archtop sound has almost nothing above 5 kHz.
Just enough air; jazz tone is mostly dry.

recipes.guitar: neck humbucker, series DK24 position 5, toggle down; tone knob 3-6; volume 7-8
recipes.playing: Pick over the end of the fretboard with a heavy, rounded pick or thumb; heavier or flatwound strings help; humbuckers set a little lower sound more acoustic.

recipes.documented_gear: Style reference: Fender Deluxe Reverb-type amp with Volume around 5-6.5 (where the 6V6 power section starts to sag), optionally pushed by a Tube Screamer.

chain.choice: Tube Screamer type (or Klon/Blues Driver type) for solos
chain.settings: boost use: drive 7-8 o'clock, tone noon, level 3 o'clock; drive use: drive 4-6, tone 5-6, level unity
chain.why: Pushes the amp over the edge and adds mids; not the main source of dirt.

chain.choice: Fender Deluxe Reverb / tweed type at the edge of breakup
chain.settings: volume ~5-6.5, treble 6-7, bass 4-5 (soft picking clean, hard picking breaks up)
chain.why: Power-amp breakup and sag give the touch sensitivity.
Part of the Fender clean voice.

chain.choice: SM57 slightly off the cap, optionally blended with a ribbon
chain.why: 57 for cut, ribbon for body.

chain.settings: low cut 80 Hz, high cut 8-10 kHz
chain.why: Keep the dynamics; avoid heavy shaping.
Classic Fender spring ambience.

recipes.guitar: neck or middle position; ride the volume DK24 position 5 or 4; volume 7-10
recipes.playing: No compressor and no gate; set the dirt with the guitar on 10, then play at 7-8 and dig in or roll up for more.

recipes.documented_gear: Style reference: single-coil guitar into a completely clean amp with a compressor in front; the MXR Dyna Comp is cited as the classic funk compressor.

chain.choice: Dyna Comp / Ross type before the amp
chain.settings: ratio ~4:1, 3-6 dB reduction, attack 15-30 ms, release 50-80 ms
chain.why: Evens up- and downstrokes while letting the pick snap through.
Classic funk colour; off for straight rhythm.

chain.choice: clean, bright, high-headroom (Fender Twin / JC type)
chain.settings: gain low, bass 3-4, mid 4-5, treble 7-8, bright on
chain.why: Must stay clean under hard strums.

chain.choice: SM57 or condenser near the cap edge
chain.why: Keeps the 2-5 kHz click.

chain.settings: low cut 100-150 Hz; +2 dB at 2-4 kHz
chain.why: Funk guitar lives above the bass guitar.
Dry keeps the rhythm tight.

recipes.guitar: in-between position, parallel DK24 position 4 (inside coils) or 2 (outer coils), toggle up; tone 10
recipes.playing: Light, consistent wrist strumming with fretting-hand muting; fresh strings matter more than any setting.

recipes.documented_gear: Style reference: Telecaster bridge pickup into a clean Fender amp (Deluxe Reverb / Super Reverb types reported by working players), light compression and a one-repeat slapback.

chain.why: Evens hybrid-picked notes and adds snap.
Bright and clean; treble deliberately high.
The signature short echo; longer or more repeats muddy it.

recipes.guitar: bridge pickup, single-coil-like DK24 position 1 with toggle up (parallel) or position 2; tone 10
recipes.playing: Pick near the bridge; hybrid picking (pick + fingers) provides the snap.

recipes.documented_gear: Roland JC-120 Jazz Chorus (its built-in stereo chorus has fixed rate and depth) and Boss CE-1/CE-2 chorus pedals are the documented reference sounds.

chain.why: The even, 'produced' attack of the era (some versions use none).
Very clean with no breakup at all.
The defining effect; stereo makes it wide.
Lush, obviously processed ambience.

chain.settings: low cut 100 Hz; high shelf +2 dB above 6 kHz
chain.why: Hi-fi sheen.

recipes.guitar: in-between or neck, parallel DK24 position 2/4 toggle up, or position 5 parallel
recipes.playing: Arpeggiated chords with open strings; pick lightly.

recipes.documented_gear: Style reference: Marshall JTM45 / 1959 Super Lead 'Plexi' turned up loud into a 4x12 (Greenback-type); guides aim JTM45 crunch settings at Zeppelin-to-AC/DC tones.

chain.why: Many Plexi players push the front end; not required.

chain.settings: volume ~7-8 (model 'gain' medium), bass 4-5, mid 7, treble 6-8, presence 6-7
chain.why: Crunch comes from the whole amp being pushed, so chords stay defined.
Woody upper-mid voice, soft top.

chain.settings: low cut 80 Hz, high cut 8-10 kHz

recipes.guitar: bridge humbucker DK24 position 1, toggle down (series); Les Paul bridge
recipes.playing: No gate, no compressor; hit hard for crunch and roll the guitar volume to 6-7 for the 'clean' sound.

recipes.documented_gear: Style reference: Marshall JCM800 with gain around 7 pushed by a Boss SD-1 (level up, gain at zero); pedals were used to boost, not saturate; chorus and delay layered on top.

chain.why: Tightens and saturates the Marshall preamp.
Mid-forward British high gain.
The 'processed' 80s sheen.

recipes.guitar: bridge humbucker, series DK24 position 1, toggle down
recipes.playing: Rhythm with less ambience; add delay, a little more level and mids for solos.

recipes.documented_gear: Per Adam 'Nolly' Getgood: modern amps have plenty of low end, so the job is controlling lows and adding midrange, typically with a Tube Screamer or Boss SD-1 in front; medium-output pickups preferred.

chain.settings: threshold just above idle noise, fast release
chain.why: Silence between staccato riffs.
Cuts bass and adds mids before the amp so the low end stays tight.

chain.settings: gain 4-6 (lower than instinct), bass 3-5, mid 5-6, treble 5-6, presence 5-6, depth ~5
chain.why: Moderate gain keeps note definition; the boost supplies attack.
Upper-mid voice that cuts through dense mixes.

chain.choice: SM57 near the cap edge (optionally + 421 or ribbon)
chain.why: 57: tight lows, presence peak.

chain.settings: low cut 80-100 Hz, high cut 8-10 kHz; -2 dB at 250-400 Hz if muddy; narrow notches at fizz peaks 4-8 kHz
chain.why: Mix-ready shape.

recipes.guitar: bridge humbucker, series DK24 position 1, toggle down; fresh strings
recipes.playing: No reverb or delay on rhythm; recorded versions are double-tracked, which supplies size with less gain.

recipes.documented_gear: Misha Mansoor: Maxon OD808 boosting the amp front end, Horizon Devices Precision Drive (signature overdrive with built-in gate), EVH 5150III and Peavey 6505+ amps (per gear listings).

chain.choice: tight gate before the boost (often a second after the preamp)
chain.why: Hard stops between notes are part of the style.
Removes lows and pushes the 1-3 kHz attack.
Low gain + mids = clarity on extended chords.
Bright, forward attack.

chain.settings: low cut 100-120 Hz, high cut 8-10 kHz, +2 dB at 1.5-2.5 kHz
chain.why: Keeps the low strings out of the bass guitar's range.

recipes.guitar: bridge humbucker, series; fresh strings DK24 position 1, toggle down
recipes.playing: Hard, precise picking with tight palm muting; low tunings need the pre-amp low cut even more.

recipes.documented_gear: Plini: Strandberg Boden Plini Edition; Neural DSP Archetype: Plini (reported as a clean, a Friedman BE-100-based crunch and a 5150-style lead amp); forum reports of Axe-Fx (Friedman HBE model) and later Quad Cortex live. Petrucci: Mesa/Boogie Mark IIC+ / JP-2C with the 5-band graphic EQ in a V (750 Hz cut deepest).

chain.why: Balances legato and tapped notes with picked ones.

chain.choice: low-gain overdrive used as a boost (Tube Screamer / Maxon type)
chain.why: Brighter, snappier front end with gain kept low.

chain.choice: Plini route: Friedman BE / 5150-style lead channel with gain LOW-MEDIUM. Petrucci route: Mark IIC+ lead
chain.settings: Plini: treble 3-4, mid 6-7, bass 3-5. Petrucci: gain 7-8, bass 1-2, mid 3-4, treble 6-7, presence 5-6 + GEQ V (80 up, 240 Hz differs between…
chain.why: Lead channel played with low gain keeps definition and dynamics; Mark tone stack is pre-gain so bass stays low and the GEQ shapes after.
Smooth top for long notes.

chain.settings: low cut 90-100 Hz, high cut 7-9 kHz

chain.why: Size and sustain.
Plini's lead is noticeably wet.

recipes.guitar: neck pickup for smooth lines, or split coils for the snappy Plini attack DK24 position 5 (series) or position 2/4; tone 8-10
recipes.playing: Low gain means the hands do the sustaining: firm fretting, clean muting. Optional light chorus on Plini-style tones.

chain.settings: tone ~9 o'clock, level ~11 o'clock, distortion ~11 o'clock
chain.why: Adds gain and upper-mid edge in front of an already slightly dirty amp; tone kept low so it stays smooth.

chain.choice: Carvin Legacy type; substitute a mid-gain, mid-forward modded-British lead amp
chain.settings: amp set 'a little dirty' on its own: gain medium, mids 6-7, treble 5-6, presence 5
chain.why: Amp supplies body, pedal supplies saturation.
Vai leads are bright but not fizzy.
Signature effect on some songs.
Width and sustain.

recipes.playing: Vai: 'The basic sound is in the tone but most important is the way you hit the notes.' Wide vibrato, bar scoops and volume-knob control are central.

recipes.documented_gear: Forum consensus for 'Europa' (Amigos, 1976): an original Mesa/Boogie Mark I-type combo run loud with high gain; one account specifies a Yamaha SG2000 into the Boogie into a single Altec 417 speaker. chain.choice: optional, only if monitoring on headphones
chain.why: Stands in for the acoustic feedback of a loud combo.

chain.choice: Boogie Mark-series lead channel (Mark I/II type)
chain.settings: gain high, mids high, treble low, bass moderate (set by ear; published numbers are unreliable)
chain.why: Cascaded-gain Boogie lead is the source of the long, smooth sustain; no overdrive pedal needed.

chain.choice: 1x12 combo with an Altec/EV-type clean, high-power speaker
chain.why: Stiff, full-range speaker keeps it fat rather than fizzy.

chain.choice: dynamic or ribbon off the cap
chain.why: Smooth top.

chain.settings: low cut 80 Hz, high cut 5-7 kHz, +2 dB at 700 Hz-1 kHz if thin
chain.why: Creamy means little above 6 kHz.
An Echoplex is mentioned for his 70s rig.

recipes.guitar: neck humbucker, series; tone rolled back Les Paul neck pickup or DK24 position 5 toggle down; tone 4-7; volume 10
recipes.playing: Sustain came from volume: Santana is said to mark stage spots where notes feed back. On headphones use more gain/compression and delay; hold notes with strong vibrato.

recipes.documented_gear: Style reference: Vox AC30-type amp at the edge of breakup, stacked low-gain drives (Tube Screamer / King of Tone / Klon types), dotted-eighth delay, big hall or shimmer reverb.

chain.why: Evens delay repeats and clean passages.

chain.settings: each drive low, level near unity; stack for more
chain.why: Gain staging in small steps keeps chords clear.

chain.settings: edge of breakup; treble moderate, bass low-moderate
chain.why: Chime plus natural compression that keeps delay repeats even.

chain.choice: dotted-eighth, tempo-synced (often a second quarter-note delay)
chain.settings: time = (60000 / BPM) x 0.75 ms; 3-5 repeats; mix 25-35%
chain.why: The rhythmic signature of the style.

chain.choice: hall plus shimmer on a parallel path
chain.why: Pads under the dry signal; parallel keeps the dry articulate.

chain.settings: low cut 100-120 Hz, high cut 7-9 kHz
chain.why: Leaves room for bass, keys and vocals.

recipes.guitar: bridge or in-between positions DK24 position 1-3; volume knob or volume pedal for swells
recipes.playing: Sparse parts, volume swells, let the repeats do the work.

recipes.documented_gear: Kevin Shields reference: detuned Jazzmasters with constant tremolo-arm movement ('glide'), reverse reverb, heavy fuzz. Sources disagree on the exact fuzz models and on whether fuzz goes before or after the reverse reverb.

chain.choice: reverse reverb BEFORE the fuzz (one school)
chain.why: The fuzz then crushes the reverb tail into a wall; the other school puts fuzz first.
Dense, sustaining wall.
Lets the pedals define the texture.
Pitch movement adds the woozy quality.
Washy on purpose.

chain.settings: low cut 100-120 Hz, high cut 6-8 kHz
chain.why: Keeps the wall from turning into fizz and mud.

recipes.guitar: any pickup; tremolo arm held while strumming DK24 position 3 or 5; floating 2-point bridge for the glide
recipes.playing: Strum full chords and work the arm; articulation is deliberately blurred.

recipes.documented_gear: Eddie Van Halen: 1968 Marshall Super Lead 'Plexi' driven hard with no distortion pedal, a Variac lowering the amp's voltage, Echoplex and MXR Phase 90 in front, 4x12 with Celestion 'blackback' speakers (JBLs also reported), close-mic'd with SM57s; humbucker-equipped 'Frankenstrat'.

chain.choice: MXR Phase 90 type before the amp
chain.why: Adds the slow mid sweep.

chain.choice: Echoplex-type tape echo before the amp
chain.why: Its preamp also colours and boosts the signal.

chain.choice: Plexi Super Lead type, everything turned up
chain.settings: gain/volume near max, mids and presence high; add sag if the model allows (the Variac effect)
chain.why: All the distortion is the amp; lowered voltage gives the soft, saggy 'brown' feel.
Speaker breakup is part of the sound.
The record has obvious studio reverb.

recipes.guitar: bridge humbucker, series DK24 position 1, toggle down; volume rolled down for cleaner parts
recipes.playing: Less preamp-style gain than it sounds; hard picking and the guitar volume knob control the dirt.

positions.sound: Hot, tight, bright with slightly scooped mids (Full Shred): fast attack, clear low strings. Series = full output; parallel = thinner, brighter, lower output, still hum-cancelling.
positions.suits: High-gain rhythm, palm mutes, pinch harmonics, crunch, cutting leads. Because the pickup is bright and mid-light, leads often want amp mids up and presence down; parallel suits twang and bright cleans.

positions.selects: Both outer coils (one coil from each pickup)
positions.sound: Widest coil spacing: airy, hollow, Tele-middle / Strat-like in parallel; a fat, wide pseudo-humbucker in series.
positions.suits: Clean arpeggios, funk, 80s cleans, snappy modern clean leads. Parallel has low output, so raise amp level or add a compressor; expect less low end, so less bass cut is needed.

positions.sound: Full but open; scooped mids with both the neck's roundness and the bridge's edge.
positions.suits: Clean chords, edge-of-breakup rhythm, jangly parts. Under high gain it can get congested; lower gain or bass.

positions.selects: Both inside coils (one coil from each pickup)
positions.sound: Closer coil spacing than position 2: a little rounder and quackier in parallel, the classic in-between notch tone.
positions.suits: Funk strumming, quack, glassy cleans, Plini-style split-coil lines with compression.

positions.sound: Warm, sweet and soft-attacked (Alnico II), moderate output; full lows, smooth top. Parallel = clearer and more single-coil-like.
positions.suits: Singing/creamy leads above the 12th fret, jazz cleans (tone rolled), legato. Under gain cut bass before the amp or it gets woofy; add presence if it turns dull.

les paul.differences: Shorter scale (24.75 in vs 25.5 in): lower string tension, easier bends, slightly warmer and less snappy, low strings less tight. Two full humbuckers with no in-between single-coil sounds: thicker low mids, more sustain and compression, smoother top. Compared with the DK24's bright, mid-light Full Shred bridge and airy split positions, a Les Paul generally puts more 200-500 Hz and less top into the same preset, and…

compensations.action: Re-check input level/gain first: play the hardest chord and match how hard the amp is being driven (trim the input or the amp gain a notch)
compensations.why: Pickup output difference changes gain, compression and noise before any EQ difference matters.

compensations.action: Raise the pre-amp low cut or boost level slightly, or lower amp Bass 1-2 notches
compensations.why: More low-mid content and a looser low string need more tightening before the distortion.

compensations.action: Cut 2-3 dB around 200-400 Hz after the amp if chords are thick
compensations.why: Les Paul low-mid build-up is the usual cause of mud in a preset made on a superstrat.

compensations.action: Add Presence/Treble 1 notch or move the mic slightly toward the cap
compensations.why: Less top end and bite than the Full Shred bridge and the no-load tone circuit.

compensations.action: For cleans made on positions 2/4, use the Les Paul's middle position, lower the guitar volume to 6-8 and reduce amp bass; add compression…
compensations.why: There is no split-coil quack; the middle position with reduced volume is the nearest substitute.

compensations.action: On the neck pickup under gain, cut more bass before the amp and consider lowering the pickup's bass side
compensations.why: Les Paul neck humbuckers are the classic source of woofy, muddy lead tones.

compensations.action: Leads may need less added mid boost and less compression
compensations.why: The guitar already supplies mids and sustain.
